title: Minimum Time to Eat All Grains
summary: Given n hens and m grains on a line, with positions in arrays hens and grains, determine the minimum time for all hens to eat all grains.
statement: Given n hens and m grains on a line, with positions in arrays hens and grains, determine the minimum time for all hens to eat all grains. Hens can move one unit in one second, either left or right, and can eat multiple grains at the same position. Hens move simultaneously and independently to minimize the total time.
constraints: Hens and grains occupy positions on a line; every hen moves at most one unit per second.
Hens move simultaneously and a hen eats every grain position it visits.
Return the minimum time needed to eat all grains.
hints: Sort both position arrays and binary-search the answer time.
For a candidate time, assign grains from left to right to hens from left to right.
When grains lie left of a hen, compare going left first with going right first to find its farthest reachable right position.
Greedily consuming the longest prefix is safe on a line; feasibility is monotone, so binary search finds the minimum time.
editorial: Greedily consuming the longest prefix is safe on a line; feasibility is monotone, so binary search finds the minimum time.

The single hen must cover both endpoints, taking six seconds by visiting one side and then the other.
